title: Tenant isolation: network and identity
purpose: Show that one team's pods cannot reach another team's pods, and that one team's job cannot read another team's data, while each can use its own.

steps.display: kubectl --context cpu-a create -f job.yaml   # vision/vision-server: queue cpu, 1 pod(s) x cpu 1
kubectl --context cpu-a create -f job.yaml   # llm/llm-probe: queue cpu, 1 pod(s) x cpu 1
kubectl --context cpu-a create -f job.yaml   # vision/vision-probe: queue cpu, 1 pod(s) x cpu 1
kubectl --context cpu-a -n llm logs job/llm-probe   # from team llm to team vision's server
kubectl --context cpu-a -n vision logs job/vision-probe   # from team vision to its own server
kubectl --context cpu-a create -f job.yaml   # llm/llm-own-data: queue cpu, 1 pod(s) x cpu 1
kubectl --context cpu-a create -f job.yaml   # llm/llm-other-data: queue cpu, 1 pod(s) x cpu 1
kubectl --context cpu-a -n llm logs job/llm-own-data   # aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/llm/dataset.txt -
kubectl --context cpu-a -n llm logs job/llm-other-data   # aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/vision/dataset.txt -

networkpolicy.networking.k8s.io/isolate-team   <none>         22m

checks.description: a pod in team llm cannot reach team vision's server
checks.because: Each team namespace has a policy that admits traffic only from its own namespace. The probe's own output says it was blocked.

checks.description: a pod in team vision can reach its own team's server
checks.because: The same policy allows pods in the same namespace. The block is deliberate, not a broken network.

checks.description: a team's job reads its own S3 prefix
checks.because: EKS Pod Identity gave the job's ServiceAccount a role limited to that team's prefix.

checks.description: the same job is refused another team's prefix
checks.because: The role's policy names only the team's own prefix. The refusal comes from IAM, not from the cluster.

notes: A server runs in team vision's namespace on cpu-a at 10.30.28.97.
